No source expansion or uncountable null-set intersection occurs.

The finite-union supremum is positive, finite and attained modulo null sets by the selected countable union; continuity from below forces every extra support into it modulo λ. Positive mixture weights then transfer Q-null sets to each Pθ without intersecting uncountably many null sets. AC covers selecting RN versions, approximating finite sets and enumerating their union. Nonempty/single-law and repeated-index cases work. Reader’s local normalization correction and supporting expansions retained.

All three steps and cited interfaces checked. Affine C1 change of variables gives each N(θ,θ²) density; independence, Tonelli and rectangle uniqueness on Borel R² give the positive product density. Expansion yields η=(u,−u²/2), A=1−2log u and Z=e/u²; the parabola has no open 2D parameter set. In-model density ratios are Borel in (S1,S2), proving sufficiency. Gaussian second moments and integrable positive/negative product terms give ES1²=6θ², ES2=4θ² and E(S1²−3S2/2)=0. The value −1/2 at (1,0), continuity, a positive density lower bound and a nondegenerate rectangle ensure nonzero probability for every θ>0. Integrability is stated and proved. Steps 1.1–3.1 prove standard-Borel measurability, common-kernel sufficiency, and coordinatewise factorization through any sufficient standard-Borel statistic S. Positive weights make Q-null sets exactly common model-null sets, and only countably many coordinate exceptional sets are combined. The original conclusion did not cover arbitrary sufficient sub-sigma-fields as required by def-minimal-sufficient-sigma-field. Clip v_A to [0,1] on H-measurable Q-null sets; simple approximation/MCT justifies testing against r_k. Then ∫_A r_k dQ=∫v_A r_k dQ=∫v_A dP_k=P_k(A), so RN uniqueness and countability give T=(r_k)_k Q-a.e., proving full minimality. AC covers RN versions; finite restriction exhaustion is X. Density verification and all cited statements checked. Translation change of variables, product-law identity, Borel product equality, Lebesgue product equality and Tonelli establish pμ on Borel R^n, treating n=1 directly. η=nμ with T=mean gives A=η²/(2n); completing the square normalizes it. Open R parameter space and null proper affine hyperplanes give full rank. Reviewed exponential-family sufficiency/completeness apply. The residual map is continuous and R_i=Z_i−mean(Z) has μ-independent joint law, so Basu applies on the standard-Borel sample R^n with standard-Borel targets R and R^n. At n=1 residual is constantly zero, still ancillary and independent. Reader’s exact product-density dependencies retained. Basu’s new sample hypothesis is met without changing this consumer.

The proof itself is sound: qC is a bounded measurable kernel evaluation, ancillarity fixes pC, completeness applies to integrable qC−pC separately for each event and parameter, and the conditional identity gives independence on every rectangle. No uniform exceptional set over all C is needed. Empty parameter family yields a vacuous conclusion, pC=0 or 1 and constant U cause no problem. No new choice is required, since sufficiency supplies K. Direct item consumer is the assigned normal example on R^n; its sample is standard Borel, so no consumer repair is required. Page reference states the qualified complete-sufficient/ancillary result without adding an outside use.
